extracted.intended_audience: prospective apprenticeship program sponsors, Registration Agencies (OA/SAAs), employers, and other stakeholders involved in registering and operating U.S. registered apprenticeship programs
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation criteria for registering and operating U.S. Department of Labor registered apprenticeship programs, including required application contents, prohibitions in apprenticeship agreements, review standards, provisional/permanent registration processes, and compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on non-compete provisions in apprenticeship agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a non-compete provision seeks to restrict the apprentice's labor market mobility, including prior to completion of the registered apprenticeship program, the inclusion of a non-compete provision is impermissible because it prevents apprentices from finding or accepting employment and undermines the portability of marketable skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: non-competes undermine workers' mobility, harm lower-income workers, and subvert the purpose of apprenticeships to provide portable skills. The Department seeks comments on how restricting non-competes would impact employers. (See discussion of prevalence, harms to hourly/low-wage workers, and FTC estimate of broader ban effects.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on non-disclosure provisions that limit future employment or filing complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.9(e) would bar including or otherwise imposing non-disclosure provisions that would have the effect of preventing the worker from working in the same field after employment ends, or that would restrict an apprentice's ability to file a complaint with a Registration Agency or other governmental body concerning violations of this part or 29 CFR part 30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: sponsors/participating employers may include NDAs that protect legitimate confidential business information or trade secrets (e.g., source code). The prohibition applies regardless of intent if the NDA would effectively restrict future employment or filing complaints. Purpose: protect apprentices' future job prospects and enable reporting of harassment/discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submission of executed apprenticeship agreements to Registration Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.9(f) would require submission of a copy of the executed apprenticeship agreement for each apprentice to the Registration Agency within 30 days of execution (reduced from 45 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements must be complete and accurate; incomplete or inaccurate submissions do not meet the requirement. For agreements covering multiple apprentices with a list of signatories, sponsors must provide an updated list of signatories within 30 days. Electronic submission via RAPIDS/Standards Builder anticipated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to cancel apprenticeship agreement during probationary period
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.9(g) retains that the apprenticeship agreement may be cancelled during the probationary period specified in the agreement by either party without cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This modifies and relocates current language; written notice requirements are addressed elsewhere (proposed §29.25(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-probation cancellation/suspension only for good cause with opportunity to cure
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.9(h) states that after the probationary period concludes: (1) the apprentice may cancel the apprenticeship agreement at any time; (2) the program sponsor may suspend or cancel the agreement only for good cause, and after reasonable opportunity for corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors must provide written notice to the apprentice explaining cause and written notice to the Registration Agency of termination. Examples of good cause: misconduct, violation of sponsor policies, continuous and documented poor performance. Department requests comments on clarifying 'good cause.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Program registration must include occupation-suitable work process schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(a)(1) requires submission of a work process schedule and related instruction outline consistent with an occupation deemed suitable for registered apprenticeship by the Administrator (per proposed §29.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA maintains an Occupation Finder Tool and sample work process schedules. If the occupation is not already deemed suitable, sponsor must request a suitability determination; OA will not review standards until suitability is approved. Administrator can require a new suitability determination if submitted work process schedule differs materially from previously approved ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory electronic submission of registration materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(a) would mandate electronic submission of program registration materials (e.g., via Standards Builder) rather than allowing non-electronic submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department expects electronic submissions to improve efficiency, timeliness, and technical assistance, enabling OA to focus more on assistance than on nonelectronic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of standards of apprenticeship and apprenticeship agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(a)(2) and (3) require that sponsors submit the standards of apprenticeship and the apprenticeship agreement for the proposed program as part of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards of apprenticeship should be consistent with proposed §29.8 and apprenticeship agreements consistent with proposed §29.9; sponsors may submit standards for multiple occupations but must include work process schedules for each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written plan for equitable recruitment and retention of apprentices
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(a)(4) would require a written plan for equitable recruitment and retention, including strategies for optimizing participation by individuals from underserved communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan may detail partnerships with pre-apprenticeship programs, workforce boards, community organizations, intermediaries, educational institutions, unions, and supportive services (childcare, transportation). Sponsors are encouraged to seek technical assistance and develop partnerships to access untapped talent pools and funding sources. Requirement applies even if not subject to part 30 affirmative action rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of financial capacity and program sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(a)(5) would require sponsors to submit information showing they possess and can maintain the financial capacity and other resources necessary to operate the proposed program on a sustained basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: narrative explaining financial planning, intent to hire and pay apprentices, wage commitments; demonstration particularly important where employers are not sponsors or programs rely on grants. OA expects disclosure of reliance on grants and long-term solvency plans; Department seeks comments on examples of acceptable submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of final agency determinations of workplace-related violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(a)(6) would require disclosure of all instances where a Federal, State, or local agency issued a final determination that the prospective sponsor (or officers/employees) violated laws regarding occupational safety and health, fair labor standards, financial mismanagement, EEO, protections against harassment or assault, or other workplace laws; the disclosure must describe the violation(s) and corrective actions taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure informs the Administrator's evaluation of whether the sponsor can provide a safe training environment. Such information could provide grounds for denial if not satisfactorily addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union participation provisions and union notice/acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(a)(7) would require inclusion of union participation provisions where apprentices are part of a collective bargaining unit. Two parts: (i) where union participates in operation of apprenticeship program, written acknowledgement or lack of objection to registration required; (ii) where no participation exists, sponsor must furnish application and program materials to the existing union representing employees and Registration Agency must allow 45 days for union comments before final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are existing requirements reorganized; purpose is to ensure appropriate union participation where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of steps to implement EEO obligations at registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(a)(8) requires sponsors to submit a description of immediate steps to implement 29 CFR 30.3(b), at minimum identifying responsible individual(s), how the EEO pledge will be published/publicized, planned schedule for EEO orientation/info sessions, current recruitment resources and contacts, and procedures for anti-harassment training and complaint handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agencies are expected to evaluate whether these elements will be implemented at time of registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application completeness requirement and 90-day review timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(b) states a complete electronic application that includes all requirements of §29.10(a) would be reviewed within 90 calendar days by the Registration Agency; the 90-day review period starts only when the application is complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure completeness to trigger the review clock. If suitability determination is required, the 90-day period does not start until suitability is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination: occupation suitability for registered apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(b)(1) requires the Registration Agency to determine that the occupation covered by the proposed program is suitable for registered apprenticeship training pursuant to proposed §29.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator may exercise discretion to determine whether the submitted work process schedule aligns with previously approved schedules and whether a new suitability determination is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination: work process schedule provides specific skills and competencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(b)(2) requires a determination that the proposed work process schedule provides training in the specific skills and competencies associated with the approved occupation as required by proposed §29.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agencies will assess alignment between the work process schedule and the occupation's required skills/competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination: portability of occupational skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(b)(3) requires a determination that the applicant's work process schedule and related instruction outline would provide an apprentice with a portable set of occupational skills and competencies readily transferable between employers within the same industry or sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portability is a key statutory purpose of registered apprenticeship; applications should demonstrate transferability across employers in the sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination: standards of apprenticeship consistency with proposed §29.8
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(b)(4) requires a determination that the standards of apprenticeship submitted are consistent with proposed §29.8 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agency will review submitted standards against the regulatory standards in §29.8; sponsors may use boilerplate standards and Standards Builder to ease compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination: apprenticeship agreement adherence to proposed §29.9
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(b)(5) requires a determination that the apprenticeship agreement adheres to the requirements of proposed §29.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes review for prohibited provisions (e.g., non-competes/non-disclosures as restricted), accurate terms, and required notice/cancellation language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination: sponsor financial capacity and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(b)(6) requires a determination that the sponsor possesses the financial capacity and other resources necessary to operate the proposed program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agency will evaluate narratives and evidence submitted under §29.10(a)(5) to conclude whether sponsor sustainability is credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination: satisfactory remediation of prior violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(b)(7) requires a determination that misconduct or violations disclosed under §29.10(a)(6) have been satisfactorily addressed and cured such that they do not pose significant ongoing risk to apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disclosures indicate unresolved or unremedied risks, the application may be denied; submissions should include corrective actions taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination: satisfaction of union participation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(b)(8) requires a determination that the union participation requirements of §29.10(a)(7) are satisfied, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agency will review union acknowledgements or evidence of notice and the 45-day comment process where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination: satisfactory equitable recruitment plan and EEO implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(b)(9) requires a determination that the sponsor's written plan for equitable recruitment and retention is satisfactory and that the application includes a satisfactory description of how EEO requirements in §29.10(a)(8) will be implemented upon registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agencies will assess whether the plan contains achievable, intentional strategies (partnerships, supportive services, outreach) and concrete implementation steps for EEO obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration outcomes, denial notice, and resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(c) provides that applications meeting required standards receive a Certificate of Registration and provisional registration; if declined, the Registration Agency must provide a written explanation of reasons and how deficiencies could be cured, and applicants may resubmit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial notices should be specific enough for sponsors to understand deficiencies and follow instructions for resubmission with new or supplemental information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional registration review and path to permanent registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(d) explains provisional registration is intended to build sponsor-Registration Agency relationships and allow technical assistance; Registration Agencies must review provisionally registered programs for compliance within 2 years of registration or at the end of the first training cycle, whichever is sooner, to determine permanent registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If found noncompliant, programs may be subject to deregistration procedures (proposed §29.20) but Registration Agencies may provide technical assistance or enhanced oversight before formal deregistration. Purpose: protect apprentices while new programs establish compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to have at least one apprentice and potential deregistration for zero apprentices
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(e) incorporates existing requirement that every registered apprenticeship program must have at least one apprentice; failure to comply may result in deregistration proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grace periods (not to exceed 1 year) apply between registration and first apprentice or between a graduation and registration of the next apprentice. Department seeks comments on whether longer 'latency' periods are appropriate and how completion metrics should be applied. Programs deregistered for zero apprentices may reregister if they meet requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to submit proposed modifications to standards to Registration Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §29.10(f) updates §29.5(b)(18) to require that any sponsor proposals for modifications or changes to standards of apprenticeship or certified National Guidelines for Apprenticeship Standards for a registered program must be submitted to the Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of modifications enables Registration Agencies to review and approve changes to ensure continued compliance with part 29 and part 30 requirements.
